results.summary: This project contains six R-C oscillators, three at 500kHz and three at 16MHz, originally designed for the Efabless Frigate project's timing subsystem. Each oscillator is enabled by a digital input and produces an output in the 1.8V domain, with four outputs on digital pins and two on analog pins. The oscillators are intended to measure cross-coupling and frequency variation across the wafer. The design is implemented with analog circuitry and has been validated on fabricated silicon.

This project is a neural network design that uses a perceptron architecture. It is implemented in Verilog and communicates via a UART interface. The design is intended for machine learning inference tasks. The documentation is sparse, but the available information indicates a digital implementation with serial communication.

This project is a simple 6-bit microcontroller built with the sky130_as_sc_hs standard cell library, intended to test that library. It includes a CPU core and uses SPI and GPIO interfaces. The design is implemented with standard cells and includes factory test structures. The documentation is incomplete, but the design appears to be a basic microcontroller for educational purposes.

This project is an LFSR-based pseudo-random number generator. It uses flip-flops and is implemented with standard cells. The design includes factory test structures. The documentation is sparse, but the design appears to be a digital circuit for generating random sequences.

This project is a memory block with an analog charge pump. It is implemented at the transistor level. The design is intended for memory applications. The documentation is sparse, but the design appears to be a custom memory circuit.

This project implements a multiplier, adder, and self-multiplier using stochastic computing. It uses LFSRs for random number generation and communicates via UART. The design is intended for DSP and neural network applications. The implementation is digital and uses stochastic computing techniques.

This project is an audio processing design that uses an I2S interface and a microphone input. It is intended for DSP applications. The design is implemented in digital logic. The documentation is sparse, but the design appears to be for audio capture or processing.

This project is a simple 8-bit CPU inspired by the esoteric language BF. It is implemented in Chisel and includes a ROM for program storage. The design uses LEDs for output and is intended for educational purposes. The CPU executes BF programs.

This project is a first test for basic IP blocks such as a PTAT (proportional to absolute temperature) sensor, oscillator, decoder, command checker, and driver, intended for microrobotics applications. The design includes analog and digital components. The documentation is sparse, but the design appears to be a test chip for various IP blocks. The capabilities and usage cannot be fully determined from the provided documentation.
